questions.prompt: Why are most modern production languages (**Python, C++, Rust, C#, Scala, Kotlin, Swift, F#**) **hybrid (multi-paradigm)**?

options.text: Language designers couldn't decide on syntax
Different problems fit different styles: OOP/components for boundaries, FP for data transforms, imperative for hot loops

questions.prompt: In **Python**, how do its three main paradigms typically work together?

options.text: Classes/protocols for domain boundaries, comprehensions/`itertools`/lambdas for transforms, and imperative scripts/methods for I/O

questions.prompt: What is **multiple dispatch** — the signature paradigm of **Julia**?

options.text: Calling one method on one receiver only
Selecting which method implementation to run dynamically based on the runtime types of **all** arguments

questions.prompt: Why is **Racket** called a 'language-oriented programming' language?

options.text: Its `#lang` system and hygienic macro tower make it easy to design custom domain-specific languages (DSLs)

questions.prompt: Select all paradigms combined in **C++** with zero-cost abstractions. (Select all that apply.)
How does **Rust** achieve memory safety without a tracing garbage collector?

options.text: By running everything in an interpreter
Via compile-time **ownership, borrowing (`&T`/`&mut T`), and lifetimes** combined with RAII

questions.prompt: Which functional features are core to idiomatic **Rust**? (Select all that apply.)
What does **LINQ** in **C#** bring to an originally OOP language?

options.text: Composable, declarative query pipelines (`Where`, `Select`, `GroupBy`) over collections and databases

code.source: evens = [x * 2 for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]

questions.prompt: Match each hybrid language to its standout multi-paradigm feature.

columns.label: Multiple dispatch + JIT for scientific computing
OOP + LINQ declarative queries + async/await + pattern matching

questions.prompt: How does **Scala** unify Object-Oriented and Functional programming?

options.text: Every value is an object and every function is an object/value, paired with case classes, traits, and typeclasses (`given`/`using`)

questions.prompt: What pragmatic improvements does **Kotlin** bring to JVM OOP/FP?

options.text: Compile-time null safety (`T` vs `T?`), data/sealed classes, extension functions, and structured coroutines

questions.prompt: What does **Protocol-Oriented Programming** in **Swift** favor over deep class inheritance?

options.text: Value types (`struct`/`enum`) conforming to protocols with protocol extensions and generics

questions.prompt: What characterizes **F#** as an 'ML-family functional-first' language on .NET?

options.text: Immutable values, type inference, discriminated unions, pipes (`|>`), and computation expressions, with full .NET OOP interop
Classes are required for every function

questions.prompt: Why is **Oz (Mozart)** famous in programming-paradigm education?

options.text: It is the fastest C compiler
It cleanly integrates declarative, stateful, OOP, concurrent dataflow, and constraint paradigms in one kernel model

questions.prompt: What is a common **anti-pattern** when writing in a hybrid language like Python or C#?

options.text: Mixing small pure functions with clear domain types
Dogmatically forcing one paradigm everywhere (e.g., 5-layer `AbstractFactory` for a 20-line script, or hidden mutation inside a `map`)

questions.prompt: What does this Python snippet demonstrate?

options.text: Structural pattern matching (`match`/`case`) over a tuple/command — bringing functional ADT-style dispatch into Python

code.source:
match cmd:
    case ('move', x, y): pos = (x, y)
    case ('quit',): done = True

questions.prompt: When is **Functional Core, Imperative Shell** the recommended architecture in a hybrid language?

options.text: Keep business rules/transforms as pure functions (easy to test) and push I/O, DB, and network side effects to a thin outer shell
Never — put SQL queries inside every pure math helper
Only when there is no database

questions.prompt: In **C#**, **Rust**, and **Swift**, why are **sealed classes / enums with associated values** replacing open class hierarchies for domain state?

options.text: Closed sum types let the compiler verify exhaustive handling of every state (e.g., `Loading | Ready | Error`)

questions.prompt: What is the **Expression Problem** in programming language design?

options.text: How to easily add **both** new data variants and new operations without modifying existing code (OOP favors new variants; FP favors new operations)

questions.prompt: How do **JavaScript / TypeScript** combine paradigms in modern web engineering?

options.text: First-class functions/closures + event-driven async (`Promise`/`async`) + prototype/class objects + immutable state patterns

questions.prompt: Select all trade-offs to weigh when choosing a paradigm for a team/system. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Number of letters in the language's name
Runtime performance & memory predictability (e.g., systems/ownership vs GC)
Team familiarity and ecosystem library fit
Concurrency/fault-tolerance model (shared-nothing actors vs locks vs async)

questions.prompt: Why do **traits** (Rust) and **protocols** (Swift) avoid the classic 'diamond problem' of C++ multiple class inheritance?

options.text: They separate behavior interfaces from shared mutable base-class state layout
They forbid having more than one method

questions.prompt: What does `std::ranges` in modern C++ (or `Iterator` chains in Rust) illustrate?

options.text: Composable, lazy functional pipelines compiled down to zero-overhead imperative loops

code.source: res = sum(x * x for x in nums if x > 0)

questions.prompt: In **Python**, why does mutating a list inside a comprehension or `map` violate good hybrid style?

options.text: It turns the list into a dict
Python forbids any function calls inside comprehensions
It breaks reader expectations of expression purity and introduces hard-to-trace side effects

questions.prompt: Match each engineering goal to the paradigm best suited for it.
What does this Python snippet (`dataclass(frozen=True)`) enforce?

options.text: An immutable value object (OOP structure + FP immutability) that is safe to share and hash

questions.prompt: What is **duck typing** vs **structural typing** vs **nominal typing**?

options.text: Duck typing checks methods at runtime; structural checks shape at compile time (TS/Go interfaces); nominal checks explicit type names/inheritance (Java/C#)
Nominal typing happens only at runtime
Duck typing only exists in C

questions.prompt: In **Swift** and **Kotlin**, what do `async`/`await` and structured concurrency simplify compared to nested callbacks?

options.text: They let asynchronous sequential steps read like linear code while scoping task lifetimes and cancellation

questions.prompt: Why might an engineer choose **Rust** or **C++** over a GC-managed hybrid language like **C#** or **Java**?

options.text: Deterministic memory/latency with zero GC pauses and direct hardware control
Because GC languages cannot do OOP

questions.prompt: What is a **monomorphization** vs **dynamic dispatch (vtable)** trade-off in Rust/C++/Swift?

options.text: Monomorphization inlines per-type code for speed at the cost of larger binary size; dynamic dispatch (`dyn Trait`/virtual) shares one code path with an indirect call

questions.prompt: Select all ways **F#** and **Scala** interoperate with their host platforms (.NET / JVM). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Sharing the host runtime's GC, profiling, and deployment tooling
Calling existing .NET or Java libraries directly
Implementing platform interfaces and classes when needed

questions.prompt: What does **extension methods/functions** (in Kotlin, C#, Swift) solve without subclassing?

options.text: Adding utility methods to existing types (even final/stdlib types) without modifying their source or creating wrapper classes

questions.prompt: In **Julia**, why does type stability in hot functions matter for JIT performance?

options.text: When variable types are inferable and stable, Julia's LLVM JIT compiles specialized machine code without boxing/dynamic dispatch overhead

questions.prompt: What does `pipe` (`|>`) in F#/Elixir or chained methods in JS/Rust improve?

options.text: Left-to-right readability of multi-step data transformations without deeply nested parentheses

questions.prompt: What is **composition over inheritance** in modern OOP/hybrid design?

options.text: Building complex behavior by combining small focused collaborator objects/functions rather than deep fragile subclass trees

questions.prompt: What does this Python snippet (`Protocol`) represent?

options.text: Static structural typing (interface satisfaction without explicit `class Foo(Greeter)`)

questions.prompt: Why do **reactive** systems (like Elm or RxJS) and **actor** systems (like Elixir) pair well with **immutable messages**?

options.text: Mutable messages are faster to debug
Immutable events/messages can be logged, replayed, and passed between concurrent stages without aliasing bugs

questions.prompt: Match each type-system mechanism to how it supports polymorphism.

columns.label: One algorithm/container parameterized uniformly over any `T`
Shared capability contract implemented per type (`Eq`, `Ord`)
Runtime selection among subtypes sharing a base/interface

questions.prompt: Select all signs that a codebase is suffering from **OOP over-engineering**. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Trivial logic split across dozens of single-implementation `ServiceImpl` / `ManagerFactory` layers
Base classes modified constantly for unrelated child needs
Small pure helper functions with unit tests
Deep inheritance trees (>3-4 levels) where subclasses override and break parent invariants

questions.prompt: What is **gradual typing** (as in TypeScript, Python type hints, or Typed Racket)?

options.text: Removing all types at runtime permanently
Allowing dynamic untyped code and static type-checked modules to coexist and migrate incrementally

questions.prompt: How does **Rust**'s `Result<T, E>` + `?` operator compare to C++/Java exceptions?

options.text: Exceptions are faster in all cases
`Result` crashes the process on every error
Errors are explicit return values in the type signature, propagated concisely with `?` without hidden stack-unwinding control paths

questions.prompt: What is the ultimate takeaway of studying multiple programming paradigms?

options.text: Mastering multiple paradigms expands how you model problems, letting you choose the cleanest mental model for any language or system
Every problem should be solved in Assembly
Only one paradigm is valid in 2026
Hybrid languages have no design principles
